subject: gk
question: Elections under which act gave the control of seven provinces in 1937 to the Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament, containing 321 sections and 10 schedules.
 
• It provided for the establishment of an **all-India federation** consisting of provinces and princely states.
 
• The Act introduced **provincial autonomy**, allowing provinces to act as separate entities with their own legislative assemblies and governments responsible to the electorate.
 
• Under this act, elections were held in 1937, leading to the Congress party gaining control of seven out of eleven provinces in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1937**

 
 
• There is no such act as the Government of India Act, 1937. The correct act is the Government of India Act, 1935, which was implemented in 1937.
 
 
 
• **Provincial Act, 1935**
 
 
• There is no separate Provincial Act, 1935. The provisions related to provincial autonomy and elections were part of the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
 
 
• **Municipalities Act, 1935**
 
 
• The Municipalities Act, 1935, is not related to the control of provinces. It generally pertains to local governance and municipal administration, not provincial autonomy or elections.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, was a crucial step toward greater self-governance in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the federal structure of government and introduced significant administrative changes.
 
• The Act also sought to address the political demands of Indian leaders by providing a larger role for Indians in governance.
 
• It led to the first provincial elections, which allowed Indian political parties to form governments in their respective provinces, marking a significant shift in colonial administration.
